newsitem.title: JAPAN: Russia C'bank mission eyes future role of PGM sale.
newsitem.headline: Russia C'bank mission eyes future role of PGM sale.

text.p: Russian central bank officials have been in talks with several Japanese trade houses this week to research Japanese precious metals market, eyeing the bank's future role as a seller of platinum group metals (PGM), local traders said on Wednesday.
They said the Russian officials are also in talks with some trade houses about possible use of gold to back bonds issued by the Moscow government.

"I heard the main aim of the visit is to research the Japanese precious metals market as the central bank could be allowed to sell a part of PGMs in the future," said a senior trader of a major trade house, which had a talk with the bank officials earlier this week.

"But it's unclear at this stage whether the bank will be able to sell PGMs this year, and it is uncertain what is going to do with the Almazjuvelireexport (Almaz)'s export quota if that happens," he said.
Currently, Almaz is Russia's sole exporter of PGMs.
Japanese traders said the Russian officials and Japanese firms have not discussed specific export contracts of PGMs.
In Moscow, however, a senior Russian central bank official said on Tuesday the bank did not intend to sell precious metals directly to Japanese customers.
Japan is the largest consumer of platinum group metals and Russia is the largest producer of palladium and one of the largest producer of platinum.
Another trader said that Russia is mulling ways to raise funds using precious metals, including PGMs and gold. But nothing concrete has been decided so far, the traders said.
Local traders said the officials were sent to Japan under instruction of First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais.
Chubais said last week Russia needed radical changes to its gold market and added that concrete proposals for liberalising it would be made within the next 10 days.
